title: CONSORT 2010 statement: extension to randomised pilot and feasibility trials
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of inadequate reporting standards for randomized pilot and feasibility trials. The authors argue that existing CONSORT guidance was designed primarily for definitive randomized controlled trials focused on efficacy or effectiveness, whereas pilot and feasibility trials have different aims—namely, assessing whether and how a future definitive RCT can be conducted. The paper therefore develops and presents an extension to the CONSORT 2010 statement specifically for randomized pilot and feasibility studies.

The approach studied is the creation of a reporting framework rather than an educational or clinical intervention. The authors describe a formal guideline-development process that included research team meetings, a modified Delphi survey, a consensus meeting, piloting of the checklist, and iterative revision. The resulting extension adapts many original CONSORT items, removes some, and adds new reporting elements specific to pilot work, such as how participants were identified and consented, progression criteria for moving to a future definitive trial, unintended consequences, and implications for progression.

The paper is not an empirical study of a single participant population. Instead, it is a methodological guidance article relevant to researchers conducting randomized pilot and feasibility trials across domains. Examples are drawn largely from health and clinical research settings, but these are illustrative rather than the focus of a new participant-based investigation.

The main conclusion is that randomized pilot and feasibility trials require reporting guidance tailored to their distinct objectives. The authors conclude that routine use of this CONSORT extension should improve the transparency, consistency, and quality of reporting for such studies, thereby helping readers judge feasibility findings appropriately and supporting the design of better future definitive randomized trials.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a reporting-guidelines/methodology paper about the CONSORT extension for randomized pilot and feasibility trials, not an empirical study of an educational intervention. It does not evaluate high-school writing feedback approaches, student outcomes, or any AI/technology intervention in K-12 education.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports no educational impact estimates, effect sizes, or student outcome findings relevant to writing quality or feedback interventions. Therefore it provides no direct evidence of impact for the target topic.
